subject: Post-incident RCA, remediation schedule, and exec commitments — Twilight Retail throughput event
messages:
From: Sara White <sara.white@twilightretail.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Urgent: sustained throughput drop and 5xx spike impacting checkout — need immediate help

Olga / Marissa —

We saw a sustained throughput degradation starting ~14:05 UTC today that caused a 30-40% drop in checkout throughput and a spike in 5xx errors for our sessionization path. Peak impact lasted ~45 minutes. This is impacting live checkout traffic in EU and US regions; GC and CS are seeing increased customer contacts. Can Redwood please:

- Confirm root cause as soon as possible
- Provide mitigation steps and ETA for stabilization
- Open an executive bridge if needed (we may escalate internally)

Attaching a short packet with Grafana snippets and a sample span. We need a timeline for remediation and whether you’ll be applying a temporary routing override.

Thanks,
Sara White
Head of Platform Engineering
Twilight Retail

Attachment: twilight_grafana_snaps.pdf (pdf)
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sara White <sara.white@twilightretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 16:25:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained throughput drop and 5xx spike impacting checkout — need immediate help

Sara —

Thanks for the heads-up and the Grafana snippets. I’ve stood up a short bridge (joining link below) with infra and runtime engineers and we’re collecting the relevant logs (please send any additional spans you can). Preliminary triage shows a surge of long-tail sessions hitting a sharded inference pool where a small subset of instances hit resource pressure; KV-cache misses amplified per-token compute.

Immediate actions we’ve started:
- Redirected 20% of Twilight traffic to additional capacity in us-west and eu-west to reduce load on the affected pool (in progress).
- Increased batching window by 10ms for checkout route to improve throughput efficiency (rolled to 10% of traffic).
- Captured full service logs and heap/disk stats (we will share artifacts).

I’m escalating to the on-call execs for visibility and will follow up with a short RCA and a set of corrective actions by EOD Monday.

Bridge: https://join.redwood.com/bridges/twilight-20270910
Olga
Olga Petrov
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: Twilight throughput drop — initial exec note and asks

FYI — summary for execs: customer impact ~45m, throughput -30–40% on checkout, elevated 5xx. Immediate mitigation applied (partial reroute + batching tweak).

Suggested exec asks:
- Approve emergency capacity (2x on-demand p2 pools) for next 48h (cost will be absorbed by incident P&L unless leadership says otherwise).
- Prioritize engineering fix for KV-cache invalidation race (root cause candidate) and a config change to improve routing thresholds.

Marissa, Jonas — can you confirm emergency capacity approval and whether we want to offer the customer a formal SLA credit? Markus — please scope the KV-cache fix and estimate ETA for PR and Canary.

O

> Sara —
> ... (message above)
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sara White <sara.white@twilightretail.com>, Alan Choi <alan.choi@twilightretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Twilight throughput incident — RCA and action plan (summary)

Sara / Alan —

Thank you for your patience. Attached is our formal RCA (twilight_rca_sept2027.pdf) and the live action tracker (also attached). Executive summary below: 

Root cause (summary):
- A race in KV-cache invalidation logic triggered during a rare resegmentation window when multiple long-lived sessions were rehydrated simultaneously. That race caused inconsistent cache state leading to a high rate of KV-cache misses.
- Misses caused increased per-token compute on a subset of sharded model instances which then caused transient overload and queuing; routing logic did not de-prioritize the affected shards quickly enough.
- The combination of serialization backpressure and slightly aggressive autoscaler thresholds resulted in a ~45 minute impact window.

Mitigations completed (Sep 10–11):
- Immediate traffic reroute to unaffected pools (partial) and extension of autoscaler headroom.
- Temporary hardening of routing thresholds to avoid reassigning requests to overloaded shards.

Corrective actions and owners (high-level):
- KV-cache race fix: Markus Klein — PR in review, ETA canary: 2027-09-20, full rollout: 2027-10-01.
- Improve shard de-prioritization: Jonas Weber — design complete, ETA canary: 2027-09-22.
- Autoscaler safe-guards: Olga Petrov & Runtime Ops — config patch applied to increase cushion; long-term change by 2027-09-30.
- Customer-facing mitigation playbook and postmortem: Marissa Cole — draft delivered and shared.

Requested customer outcomes:
- Confirm whether Twilight wants formal SLA credit (we will prepare a credit proposal).
- Verify acceptance criteria for final rollout and propose a joint verification window (we recommend 72h monitoring after rollout).

Attached: twilight_rca_sept2027.pdf, twilight_action_tracker_sep2027.xlsx, service_logs_20270910.tgz

We’ll run a short readout with execs and your engineering leads tomorrow at 13:00 UTC to walk through the RCA and the corrective timeline; agenda and invites shortly.

Olga
From: Alan Choi <alan.choi@twilightretail.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara White <sara.white@twilightretail.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 08:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Twilight throughput incident — RCA and action plan (summary)

Olga / Marissa —

Thanks for the RCA and the quick mitigations. Two asks from Twilight: 
1) Please provide the formal SLA credit calculation and contract reference (our procurement will need the line item).
2) Can you confirm the plan to validate the fix in our staging (we prefer a shared verification, not unilateral) and propose a 72h monitoring window after rollout.

Also, given the customer impact and support overhead, our CISO asked if you can share the service logs earlier (we saw the logs were attached but would like a sanitized subset to share with our audit team).

Alan
Director of Product Ops
Twilight Retail
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alan Choi <alan.choi@twilightretail.com>, Sara White <sara.white@twilightretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Twilight throughput incident — RCA and action plan (summary) — actions and closure timeline

Alan / Sara —

Follow-up after the readout:
- SLA credit: Marissa will send a formal credit calculation by EOD Monday with contract paragraph references. We are prepared to propose a pro-rated credit for the impacted window per section 4.2 of the SOW.
- Shared verification: Markus will deploy the KV-cache fix to Twilight staging on 2027-09-20 and invite your engineers to the canary. We request a 72h joint monitoring window after canary success; exact dates to be coordinated in the invite.
- Logs: We’ll provide a sanitized logs bundle for your audit team by Monday; sensitive fields redacted.

Action status snapshot: 
- KV-cache PR: in review (Markus) — ETA canary 2027-09-20.
- Shard de-prioritization PR: ready for canary 2027-09-22 (Jonas).
- Autoscaler policy: soft fix deployed, long-term change tracked in action tracker (Olga).

Link to action tracker (live): https://docs.redwood.com/drive/twilight-action-tracker-2027
Attachments: twilight_action_tracker_sep2027.xlsx (current status).

We will follow through on the monitoring window and then provide a final close email after the joint verification completes. Thank you for working with us on this — we take this seriously and will ensure the measures prevent recurrence.

Olga Petrov
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
